# Introduction

Mumbai is the financial capital of India. Mumbai is also the most densely
populated city in India, with more than 20 million residents. Because Mumbai is
on the coast, it has better natural ventilation than Delhi, which is landlocked.
But the PM2.5 levels in Mumbai are regularly more than the WHO safe limits. The
causes are vehicle emissions, industrial activity, construction dust, and
seasonal sea-salt aerosols.

This vignette uses two different data sources in the `vayuayan` package for
an analysis of the air quality of Mumbai in 2022. Together, the two sources
help with one policy question:

> Do the 30 CPCB ground monitoring stations give sufficient coverage of the
> full spatial extent of pollution in Mumbai? Or do some localities have an
> insufficient number of monitors? If so, is the PM2.5 of these localities
> systematically missing from the network data?

The analysis has four steps:

1. The seasonal trend shows if the satellite data and the ground data agree on
   the pollution cycle of Mumbai.
2. The spatial heatmap shows where pollution in Mumbai is highest.
3. The station network map shows the locations of the 30 sensors in relation
   to that pollution.
4. The gap analysis finds the localities that are farthest from their nearest
   sensor. The gap analysis also finds if that distance predicts the
   disagreement between ground data and satellite data.

---

# Data and methods

## Satellite data

The monthly PM2.5 estimates come from the V5GL04 product of the Washington
University in St. Louis Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (WUSTL ACAG).
V5GL04 is a global gridded dataset at ~0.01° (~1 km) resolution. The dataset
uses satellite retrievals of aerosol optical depth, chemical transport models,
and ground-level calibration (van Donkelaar et al., 2021). The files are in NetCDF
format.

V5GL04 has data for 1998 to 2022. For 2023 and the years after 2023, you must
use V6GL02. At this time, the departmental server does not have the V6GL02
download. This vignette uses 2022 data in all sections.

## Ground data

`cpcb_download_city_data()` and `cpcb_download_station_data()` get the daily
city-level and per-station PM2.5 readings from the Central Pollution Control
Board (CPCB) data repository. Mumbai has 30 registered CAAQMS stations. MPCB,
IITM, and BMC operate these stations. `cpcb_add_coords()` gets the station
coordinates directly from the CPCB live feed. The function uses Nominatim as an
alternative source only for the stations that are temporarily not in the live
feed.

12 of the 30 registered Mumbai stations have no downloadable historical data in
the CPCB repository for any year. But these stations are in the station
registry. MPCB and BMC operate these 12 stations. These stations are in
central, western, and eastern Mumbai.

Thus, the delta map uses only the 18 stations with 2022 readings. The priority
map uses all 29 stations with valid coordinates. The analysis does not include
one station (`site_5102`, Vasai West). This station is outside the Mumbai city
limits, in Palghar district.

## Spatial units

The GeoJSON boundary file
(`geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/greater_mumbai.geojson`) has 227
localities in the 24 administrative wards of Mumbai (codes A to T). Each
locality is in one ward. All spatial analysis is at the locality level. The
maps show the ward boundaries as a reference.

## Limits of the comparison

The two data sources measure PM2.5 differently:

- A satellite value is the spatial mean over a full area (~1 km pixels).
- A ground value is a point measurement at one physical location. Ground
  stations are frequently near pollution sources.

Thus, the ground readings are consistently higher than the satellite estimates.
This difference is the result of a point measurement compared with an
area-averaged measurement. The difference is not an error. To compare the two
sources in time correctly, the analysis calculates monthly means from the
ground data.

---

# Setup

```{r packages}
library(vayuayan)
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(tidyterra)
library(exactextractr)
library(ncdf4)
library(khroma)
library(scales)
```

```{r folder-setup}
vignettes_dir <- here::here("vignettes")
data_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "data/mumbai")
fig_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "figures/mumbai")
station_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "station_data_mumbai")

for (d in c(data_dir, fig_dir, station_dir)) {
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
```

## Satellite files

The satellite values come from WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 monthly files. The package
downloads these files (Asia subset) one time from the AWS Open Data registry
into `nc_dir`. `pm25_monthly()` gives the mean over the bounding box of a
region. `pm25_load_netcdf_bbox()` gives the cropped raster.

```{r nc-dir}
nc_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "data/pm25")
```

---

# Results

## Seasonal trend

### Ground data: city-level monthly PM2.5

```{r ground-data}
# Cached to data/mumbai/, so re-runs skip the download
mumbai_ground <- cpcb_city_daily("Mumbai", 2022, cache_dir = data_dir) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(value), .groups = "drop")

print(mumbai_ground)
```

### Satellite data: monthly spatial mean over Mumbai

```{r satellite-data}
mumbai_shape <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/greater_mumbai.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

mumbai_sat_df <- pm25_monthly(mumbai_shape, 2022, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir) %>%
  rename(sat_pm25 = pm25)

mumbai_final <- inner_join(mumbai_ground, mumbai_sat_df, by = "month")
print(mumbai_final)
```

### Seasonal line chart

```{r line-chart, fig.cap="Mumbai 2022: monthly PM2.5 from satellite and ground sources. Both sources agree on the seasonal pattern, with a peak in winter and a minimum in the monsoon. Ground readings are consistently higher because of the difference between point and area measurement (refer to Data and methods)."}
ggplot(mumbai_final, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite"),
    linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite"), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", color = "orange", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 1, y = 18, label = "WHO 24hr limit (15 µg/m³)",
    size = 3, color = "tan4", hjust = 0
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 1, y = 8, label = "WHO annual limit (5 µg/m³)",
    size = 3, color = "darkgreen", hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "CPCB Ground"     = "#d77027ff",
    "WUSTL Satellite" = "#4575b4"
  )) +
  labs(
    title   = "Mumbai 2022: PM2.5 seasonal cycle, satellite vs ground",
    y       = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    x       = NULL,
    color   = NULL,
    caption = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS | Dotted lines = WHO guidelines"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text               = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey85"),
    legend.position    = "top"
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig1_mumbai_seasonal_trend.png"), width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

The line chart shows a clear seasonal cycle in Mumbai. PM2.5 is highest from
October to January. PM2.5 decreases by a large quantity during the southwest
monsoon (June to September). In Mumbai, heavy rain cleans the air, and PM2.5 in
the monsoon months comes near safe levels. Delhi does not have this effect.

For 2023 to 2025, ground data is available. At this time, the satellite data
for these years (V6GL02) is not on the departmental server.

## Spatial heatmap

```{r heatmap-data}
nov_file <- pm25_download_netcdf(2022, 11, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir)
r_nov <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, mumbai_shape)
mumbai_raster_mask <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, mumbai_shape, mask = TRUE)
mumbai_city_boundary <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_union(mumbai_shape))
```

```{r heatmap, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Spatial PM2.5 distribution across Mumbai, November 2022. Blue outline = Mumbai city boundary. Northern suburbs usually have higher PM2.5 than the southern peninsula."}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = mumbai_raster_mask) +
  geom_sf(
    data      = mumbai_city_boundary,
    fill      = NA,
    color     = "royalblue4",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette  = "muted",
    na.value = NA,
    name     = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Spatial distribution of PM2.5 in Mumbai",
    subtitle = "Satellite estimate: November 2022",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 | Resolution: ~1 km"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig2_mumbai_heatmap_nov2022.png"), width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

The heatmap shows higher pollution in the northern suburbs (Kandivali,
Borivali, Malad, Andheri) than in the southern peninsula (Colaba, Fort). This
result agrees with the higher industrial activity, traffic density, and
construction in the north.

## Station network choropleth

### Load station locations

```{r station-coords}
# Cached to data/mumbai/; re-runs use the cache
station_file <- file.path(data_dir, "mumbai_stations_with_coords.csv")
if (file.exists(station_file)) {
  mumbai_station_list <- read.csv(station_file)
} else {
  mumbai_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Mumbai")
  mumbai_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(mumbai_station_list)
  # Remove site_5102: Vasai West, outside Mumbai city limits (Palghar district)
  mumbai_station_list <- mumbai_station_list %>% filter(value != "site_5102")
  write.csv(mumbai_station_list, station_file, row.names = FALSE)
}

mumbai_full_sf <- mumbai_station_list %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), value != "site_5102") %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(mumbai_full_sf), "stations loaded\n")
```

### Choropleth: locality-level PM2.5 and station locations

```{r choropleth-data}
mumbai_localities <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/greater_mumbai.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

mumbai_localities$sat_pm25 <- exactextractr::exact_extract(
  r_nov, mumbai_localities, "mean",
  progress = FALSE
)
```

```{r choropleth, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Locality-level satellite PM2.5 with CPCB station locations. Blue dots = CPCB stations with 2022 data. Most stations are in south and central Mumbai."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = mumbai_localities, aes(fill = sat_pm25),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = mumbai_full_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "royalblue4",
    size = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value  = "grey80",
    name      = expression(paste("Sat PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Mumbai PM2.5 monitoring network",
    subtitle = "Locality shading = satellite average PM2.5 | Blue dots = CPCB stations",
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig3_mumbai_choropleth_stations.png"), width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

The choropleth shows that most stations are in south and central Mumbai.
Some northern localities have high PM2.5 but only a small number of sensors.
Most of these localities are in wards R and S.

---

## Monitoring gap analysis

### Per-station winter ground data

```{r winter-ground}
# Per-station 2022 data, averaged over winter months: Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan
# Station CSVs cached to station_data_mumbai/
station_ground <- cpcb_station_daily(
  mumbai_station_list$value, 2022,
  cache_dir = station_dir
) %>%
  filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12)) %>%
  group_by(station_id) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(value), .groups = "drop")

station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%
  left_join(mumbai_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon),
    by = c("station_id" = "value")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), station_id != "site_5102") %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5 (2022 data)\n")
cat("Note: 12 of 30 stations have no downloadable data in the CPCB repository\n")
```

### Compute delta at each locality centroid

```{r compute-delta}
locality_centroids <- sf::st_centroid(mumbai_localities)

sat_centroid_vals <- terra::extract(r_nov, terra::vect(locality_centroids))
mumbai_localities$sat_pm25_centroid <- sat_centroid_vals[, 2]

dist_matrix_winter <- sf::st_distance(locality_centroids, station_ground_sf)
nearest_idx <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, which.min)

mumbai_localities$nearest_ground_pm25 <- station_ground_sf$ground_pm25[nearest_idx]
mumbai_localities$nearest_winter_km <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, min) / 1000

# Delta = satellite at locality centroid − nearest station ground reading
# All values expected to be negative; ground stations read higher (point-source bias)
# Analysis focuses on *relative* disagreement across localities
mumbai_localities$delta <- mumbai_localities$sat_pm25_centroid -
  mumbai_localities$nearest_ground_pm25

mumbai_localities <- mumbai_localities %>%
  mutate(
    priority = case_when(
      nearest_winter_km > 2 & sat_pm25_centroid > median(sat_pm25_centroid, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_winter_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

cat("Delta summary (satellite - nearest ground station):\n")
print(summary(mumbai_localities$delta))
cat("\nPriority breakdown:\n")
print(table(mumbai_localities$priority))
```

### The monitoring gap map

```{r gap-map, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Monitoring gap map. The color of each locality shows the ground-satellite disagreement. Dashed lines connect each locality centroid to its nearest CPCB station. Yellow dots = CPCB stations with 2022 data (18 of 30)."}
centroid_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(locality_centroids)
station_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(station_ground_sf)[nearest_idx, ]

connection_lines <- data.frame(
  x_from = centroid_coords[, 1],
  y_from = centroid_coords[, 2],
  x_to   = station_coords[, 1],
  y_to   = station_coords[, 2],
  delta  = mumbai_localities$delta
) %>% filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = mumbai_localities, aes(fill = delta),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = connection_lines,
    aes(x = x_from, y = y_from, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
    color = "grey8", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = station_ground_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = khroma::colour("roma")(100),
    values = scales::rescale(c(
      min(mumbai_localities$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      median(mumbai_localities$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(mumbai_localities$delta, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Mumbai: satellite vs nearest ground station PM2.5 by locality",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines connect each locality centroid to its nearest CPCB station\nYellow = CPCB stations with 2022 data (18 of 30 registered stations)",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite PM2.5 at locality centroid − nearest CPCB station reading\nNovember 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig4_mumbai_monitoring_gap_map.png"), width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

### Priority map

```{r priority-map, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Priority localities for new CPCB stations in Mumbai. Red = high pollution and poor sensor coverage (>2 km from nearest station). The priority map uses all 29 stations with valid coordinates."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = mumbai_localities, aes(fill = priority),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = mumbai_full_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 3, shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "High priority"   = "#d6604d",
      "Medium priority" = "#fdae61",
      "Well monitored"  = "#4dac26"
    ),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Monitoring priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Mumbai: priority localities for new CPCB monitoring stations",
    subtitle = "Red = above-median PM2.5 and >2 km from nearest sensor\nOrange = >2 km from sensor | Green = well covered | Yellow = existing stations (29)",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS | November 2022"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig5_mumbai_priority_map.png"), width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

### Sensor distance vs disagreement

```{r scatter, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Relation between sensor distance and ground-satellite disagreement across 227 Mumbai localities. The LOESS fit shows the non-linear trend."}
cor_val <- cor(
  mumbai_localities$nearest_winter_km,
  abs(mumbai_localities$delta),
  use = "complete.obs"
)
cat("Correlation (distance vs |delta|): r =", round(cor_val, 3), "\n")

ggplot(
  data = sf::st_drop_geometry(mumbai_localities),
  aes(x = nearest_winter_km, y = abs(delta))
) +
  geom_point(aes(color = nearest_winter_km), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(mumbai_localities$nearest_winter_km, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.55,
    y = max(abs(mumbai_localities$delta), na.rm = TRUE) * 0.92,
    label = paste0("r = ", round(cor_val, 2)),
    size = 4.5, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_distiller(
    palette   = "RdYlGn",
    direction = -1,
    name      = "Distance to\nnearest sensor (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sensor distance predicts ground-satellite disagreement",
    subtitle = "Each point = one Mumbai locality (n = 227) | LOESS fit with 95% CI",
    x        = "Distance to nearest CPCB station (km)",
    y        = expression(paste("|Delta| PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3))),
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig6_mumbai_distance_vs_disagreement.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Discussion

## Seasonal pattern

The seasonal PM2.5 cycle of Mumbai is different from the cycle of Delhi (refer
to the seasonal line chart). The southwest monsoon (June to September) causes
heavy rain. The rain removes a large quantity of particulates from the air. As
a result, PM2.5 comes near safe levels in some months. In the dry winter months
(October to January), PM2.5 increases by a large quantity. In these months,
northeast monsoon winds supply dry continental air, and temperature inversions
keep pollutants near the surface.

## Spatial differences

The heatmap shows a clear north-south gradient. The northern suburbs have
higher satellite PM2.5 than the southern peninsula. This gradient agrees with
the concentration of industrial zones, construction activity, and traffic
corridors in the north. The southern peninsula receives sea breezes from three
sides.

## Monitoring gap

The gap analysis finds the localities where the 30-station network can give
incomplete data at this time. Some localities have long lines from the
centroid to the station on the gap map. For these localities, the risk is
highest that the network data shows PM2.5 values that are too low. This risk
is highest in the outer northern wards.

---

# Limitations

- The delta values are negative. Ground stations consistently give higher values
  than satellite estimates. The cause is the point-source bias: the stations
  are near pollution sources. Thus, the analysis uses the *relative*
  disagreement across localities. The analysis does not use the absolute
  values.

- 12 of the 30 registered Mumbai stations have no downloadable historical data
  in the CPCB repository for any year. But these stations are in the station
  registry. MPCB and BMC operate these stations. These stations are in central,
  western, and eastern Mumbai. Thus, the delta map uses only the 18 stations
  with 2022 readings. The priority map uses all 29 stations with valid
  coordinates.

- `site_5102` (Vasai West) is outside the Mumbai city limits, in Palghar
  district. No spatial analysis includes this station.

- The satellite data version V5GL04 has data for 1998 to 2022. When the new
  version is available, you can use the same method for all years.

- Mumbai has an irregular coastline. Thus, some locality polygons can include
  areas of sea. These areas of sea have a small effect on the area-weighted
  extraction of PM2.5.
